channel.title: AI Campaign News (AICN)
channel.description: A tracker of AI use in political campaigns, elections, and advocacy.

item.title: Grassroots Analytics is Acquiring Quiller AI
item.description: Grassroots Analytics announced it is acquiring Quiller AI, a generative AI fundraising tool, with the goal of integrating Quiller's AI copywriting capabilities into Grassroots Analytics' progressive donor data and segmentation platform to create an all-in-one AI fundraising product.

item.title: States rush to police AI deepfakes ahead of midterm elections
item.description: Marketplace reported that states are accelerating efforts to regulate AI-generated deepfakes in political content ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, reflecting a broader push to address synthetic media in campaigns before November.

item.title: AI Becomes a Major Election Issue for the First Time
item.description: Political Wire flags a Washington Post report finding that hundreds of House, Senate, and gubernatorial candidates are actively engaging with AI as a campaign issue, with AI and data centers appearing on more candidate websites than Israel or manufacturing. The piece frames 2026 as the first election cycle in which AI has featured widely as a political issue rather than merely a campaign tool.

item.title: Q&A: California’s Top Politics Watchdog on AI and Influencers
item.description: Campaigns & Elections published a Q&A with California Fair Political Practices Commission Chair Adam Silver exploring how the agency is thinking about AI-generated political content and influencer disclosures, including the tension between free speech and campaign finance regulation. Silver addresses what the FPPC is watching and how it may act on new campaign technology frontiers.

item.title: Election Briefing: Artificial Intelligence: What Campaigns Are Already Doing, and What They Should Be Ready for Between Now and Election Day
item.description: Campaigns & Elections published a practitioner-facing briefing drawing on strategist conversations about where campaigns are getting the most value from AI in the 2026 midterm cycle — covering current adoption patterns and the fault lines practitioners will need to navigate before November.

item.title: aKillion and Subtext Form a Strategic Partnership and Introduce IONCandidate, the Real-Time AI Platform That Converts Constituent Text Messages Into Political Campaign Engagement, Revenue, and Voter Action
item.description: aKillion and Subtext announced a strategic partnership and the launch of IONCandidate, a conversational AI platform built specifically for political campaigns that converts inbound constituent text messages into engagement, fundraising, and voter action in real time.

item.title: Scott Wiener's AI chatbot controversy, explained
item.description: Axios San Francisco reported on controversy surrounding California State Senator Scott Wiener's AI chatbot, with critics raising concerns about the chatbot's behavior or outputs in the context of his political profile.

item.title: Bruce Blakeman has defiant message for Dems angry about his AI ads on Hochul , Mamdani
item.description: Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman responded defiantly to Democratic criticism of his AI-generated campaign ads depicting Kathy Hochul and Zohran Mamdani, defending the ads as legitimate political speech.

item.title: As Dems move to stop Blakeman AI depictions , he calls foul
item.description: New York Democratic Party Chair Jay Jacobs filed a complaint with the state Board of Elections alleging that Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman's campaign violated state law by running AI-generated depictions of Hochul and Mamdani.

item.title: Blakeman used public funds for AI ads , Dems say | Political
item.description: The Daily Gazette reports that New York State Democrats accused Bruce Blakeman of using public funds to produce AI-generated campaign ads targeting Hochul and Mamdani, adding a potential misuse-of-public-funds dimension to the complaint.

item.title: Democrats' AI strategy is MIA
item.description: Axios reports that Democrats lack a coherent AI strategy for the 2026 cycle, leaving the party without a unified approach to adopting or countering AI-driven campaign tools.

item.title: What Campaigns Need To Know About AI Polling
item.description: The Centre for Campaign Innovation published a practitioner-facing overview of AI-generated polling, noting that startups are selling synthetic surveys to campaigns and that established firms like Gallup and Ipsos have begun validating the concept.

item.title: Civly Politics | AI Campaign Intelligence Platform for Political Campaigns
item.description: Civly launched Civly Politics, an AI campaign intelligence platform offering synthetic polling, FEC compliance and donor verification, fundraising CRM, and opposition research tools targeted at political campaigns.

item.title: NGP VAN Launches NGP VAN Interface, Bringing Agentic AI to Democratic and Progressive Campaigns Ahead of Midterm Elections
item.description: NGP VAN announced the launch of NGP VAN Interface, an agentic AI product integrated into its campaign management platform and targeted at Democratic and progressive campaigns ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence Is Taking Over Political Campaigns - The Daily Signal
item.description: The Daily Signal published a survey-style piece arguing that AI tools are dominating 2026 midterm campaign operations — not merely as a policy debate topic — covering adoption of AI in voter targeting, messaging, and field work.

item.title: Viamedia.ai Adds Aristotle Political Intelligence to Geo-Graph™, Giving Campaigns Neighborhood-Level Precision and Incremental Voter Reach
item.description: Viamedia.ai announced the integration of Aristotle Political Intelligence into its Geo-Graph platform, enabling campaigns to target swing voters, low-propensity supporters, and custom donor audiences down to the block level with real-time ad activation.

item.title: IQM DEBUTS VOTERTV+: A PRECISION POLITICAL SUITE ENGINEERED FOR DEDUPLICATED REACH AND THE VOTERS LINEAR TV CAN'T TOUCH
item.description: IQM Advertising Corporation launched VoterTV+, a cross-screen political ad planning suite that combines linear TV and digital in a single workspace, allowing campaigns to model audience reach and deduplicated voter contact before committing budget.

item.title: AI Voter Targeting Strategies for 2026 Campaigns
item.description: The Political Group published a practitioner-facing overview of how AI-driven voter targeting is being used in 2026 campaigns, covering strategy, risk considerations, and the trajectory of intelligent targeting tools.

item.title: Opinion : Artificial intelligence is moving fast while Alaska policy stands still
item.description: An op-ed in the Anchorage Daily News argues that Alaska has failed to enact any comprehensive AI legislation or data-center policy while other states are adopting consumer, worker, and child protections tied to AI — leaving the state without a regulatory framework as the technology accelerates.

item.title: AI is getting better at election facts, but voters shouldn't rely on it
item.description: New research finds that AI chatbots have meaningfully reduced factual errors when answering election-related questions ahead of the 2026 midterms, but incomplete or partial answers remain a significant risk for voters who rely on them for electoral information.

item.title: Voters face uneven AI deepfake protections
item.description: Axios reports that voters heading into the 2026 midterms face a highly uneven landscape of state-level legal protections against AI-generated deepfakes in political content, with significant gaps across many states.

item.title: Why AI giants' political spending could balloon this fall
item.description: NBC News reports that major AI companies are expected to significantly increase their political spending ahead of the fall 2026 general elections, driven by high-stakes fights in Congress and statehouses over AI regulation, data center permitting, and related policy battles.

item.title: How the booming backlash to AI data centers is shaping the midterm election
item.description: NBC News documents how community backlash to rapid hyperscale AI data center construction — touching on power consumption, land use, and water — emerged as a live campaign issue in 2025 state elections and is now rippling into 2026 midterm races up and down the ballot.

item.title: Democrats’ Split on AI Grows as a New Plan Emerges
item.description: NOTUS reports that Senate Democrats are increasingly divided on AI policy, with Senate Finance Committee ranking member Ron Wyden introducing a proposal to tax data centers as part of a broader intra-party dispute over how to approach AI regulation and industry incentives.

item.title: We're headed toward the first true AI election
item.description: Axios argues that 2026 and 2028 are poised to become the first elections meaningfully defined by AI, pointing to the growing use of campaign bots and simulated voters as evidence of a structural inflection point in electoral politics.

item.title: AI-generated political ad in St. Charles County raises deepfake questions ahead of primary election
item.description: A fully AI-generated political ad targeting candidates in the St. Charles County executive race drew scrutiny over the role of deepfakes in local elections, with the story published two weeks before the primary.

item.title: Exclusive: The AI 'news' accounts hyping a blue-state dystopia
item.description: Semafor reports that AI-generated video accounts on YouTube are flooding the platform with fabricated narratives portraying chaos in California and New York, presenting fictional content as news to advance a partisan political framing.

item.title: Mark Cuban says the winners of the 2026 midterms are those 'already working' to integrate AI into their campaigns
item.description: Mark Cuban told Business Insider that the winners of the 2026 midterms will be campaigns that are already integrating AI tools such as ChatGPT and Gemini into their operations.

item.title: Imagining Two Possible Futures of AI In Political Campaigning
item.description: The Center for Campaign Innovation published a piece exploring two contrasting scenarios for how AI could reshape political campaigning, framing potential trajectories rather than reporting on a specific deployment.

item.title: Brazil banned Bolsonaro from speaking . His AI avatar spoke anyway .
item.description: Despite a legal ban on Jair Bolsonaro speaking publicly, an AI-generated video avatar of the jailed former Brazilian president addressed a campaign rally in São Paulo at the launch of his son Flávia's presidential bid, circumventing the court order.
